title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 12.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 12, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual gifts
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with a discussion about spiritual gifts as stated in 1 Corinthians 12:1.

questions.question: What does Paul say about the Gentiles in 1 Corinthians 12?
options: They were led to dumb idols
questions.correctAnswer: They were led to dumb idols
questions.explanation: Paul states in 1 Corinthians 12:2 that the Gentiles were carried away unto these dumb idols.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12, who can call Jesus the Lord?
options: No man speaking by the Spirit of God
questions.correctAnswer: No man speaking by the Spirit of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:3 clearly states that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed, and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 12:4 say about gifts?
questions.correctAnswer: There are diversities of gifts
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:4 states that there are diversities of gifts but the same Spirit.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 12:5 state about administrations?
questions.correctAnswer: There are many administrations
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:5 mentions that there are differences of administrations, but the same Lord.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'same God' refer to in 1 Corinthians 12:6?
options: Same God working all in all
questions.correctAnswer: Same God working all in all
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:6 states that it is the same God which worketh all in all.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12:7, who receives the manifestation of the Spirit?
questions.correctAnswer: Every man
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:7 states that the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.

questions.question: What is one of the gifts mentioned in 1 Corinthians 12:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Word of wisdom
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:8 states that to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 12:9 say is given by the same Spirit?
questions.correctAnswer: Faith
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:9 mentions that to another is given faith by the same Spirit.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 12:10 list as one of the gifts?
questions.correctAnswer: Discerning of spirits
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:10 includes discerning of spirits as one of the gifts given.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12:11, who divides the gifts?
questions.correctAnswer: The selfsame Spirit
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:11 states that all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will.

questions.question: Is it stated that the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:7 states that the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man.

questions.question: Does Paul mention divers kinds of tongues in 1 Corinthians 12?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:10 lists divers kinds of tongues as one of the gifts.

questions.question: 1 Corinthians 12 states that all gifts are the same.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:4 states that there are diversities of gifts, indicating they are not all the same.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12, Jesus is the Lord only by the Holy Spirit.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:3 implies that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord but by the Holy Ghost, but it does not state that Jesus is the Lord only by the Holy Spirit.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12:12, what is the relationship between the many members and the body?
options: All the members of that one body, being many, are one body
Each member acts independently from the body
The body is made up of only a few important members
The body has many members but they are separate
questions.correctAnswer: All the members of that one body, being many, are one body
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:12 states that all the members of that one body, though many, are one body, showing unity among diversity.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 12:13 promise will happen if someone is baptized by one Spirit into one body, as commanded in verse 12?
options: They will all be made to drink into one Spirit
They will no longer be members of the body
questions.correctAnswer: They will all be made to drink into one Spirit
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:13 explains that by one Spirit we are all baptized into one body and have been all made to drink into one Spirit, fulfilling the unity described in verse 12.

questions.question: What does Paul use as a metaphor to explain the unity and diversity within the church in 1 Corinthians 12:14?
options: The body is not one member, but many
The church is like a building
The church is like a family
The body has only one important member
questions.correctAnswer: The body is not one member, but many
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:14 states that the body is not one member but many, illustrating the diversity within unity.

questions.question: How do 1 Corinthians 12:15 and 1 Corinthians 12:16 together demonstrate the relationship between different members of the body?
options: Different members should not feel less important because they differ from others
Only the hand and eye are necessary
Members can reject each other if they are different
questions.correctAnswer: Different members should not feel less important because they differ from others
questions.explanation: Verses 15 and 16 show the foot and ear saying they are not of the body because they are not the hand or eye, but Paul argues this is not true, emphasizing the value of all members.

questions.question: What question does Paul ask in 1 Corinthians 12:17 to emphasize the need for different senses in the body?
options: If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing?
Is the eye more important than the hand?
Can the body live without the heart?
Why do some members feel unnecessary?
questions.correctAnswer: If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:17 asks if the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be, highlighting the necessity of different members with distinct functions.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12:18, who determines the placement of members in the body?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:18 says God has set the members every one of them in the body as it pleased Him, showing divine sovereignty.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 12:19 imply would happen if all members were the same?
options: The body would be more beautiful
The body would be more efficient
questions.correctAnswer: There would be no body
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:19 states that if all were one member, where were the body, implying the body depends on diversity to exist as a whole.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 12:20 describe the nature of the members and the body?
options: They are many members, yet one body
They are fewer members but stronger
questions.correctAnswer: They are many members, yet one body
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:20 confirms that members are many but together form one body, emphasizing unity in diversity.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 12:21, what is the relationship between the eye and the hand?
options: The eye cannot say to the hand, I have no need of thee
The eye is more important than the hand
The hand is independent of the eye
The eye ignores the hand’s function
questions.correctAnswer: The eye cannot say to the hand, I have no need of thee
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:21 teaches that members of the body need each other and none should regard another as unnecessary.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12:22, which members of the body are described as necessary?
options: Those which seem to be more feeble
questions.correctAnswer: Those which seem to be more feeble
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:22 states that the members which seem to be more feeble are necessary, emphasizing that all members have value.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 12:12 teach about the unity of the church in relation to Christ?
options: Christ is separate from the church
The church is divided from Christ
questions.correctAnswer: So also is Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:12 concludes that just as the body is one with many members, so also is Christ, indicating unity with Him.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 12:13 describe the inclusivity of the body of Christ?
options: Whether we be Jews or Gentiles, bond or free
Only Jews can be part of the body
questions.correctAnswer: Whether we be Jews or Gentiles, bond or free
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:13 states that by one Spirit we are all baptized into one body regardless of ethnic or social status.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 12:21, the head can say to the feet, 'I have no need of you.'
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:21 explicitly says the eye cannot say to the hand, nor the head to the feet, 'I have no need of you,' showing mutual dependence.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 12:22 states that the strongest members are the only necessary parts of the body.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:22 teaches that those members which seem to be more feeble are necessary, not just the strongest members.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 12:19, if all members were the same, the body would still be complete and whole.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:19 states that if they were all one member, where were the body, indicating the body would not be whole without diversity.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 12.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12:23, which members of the body do we bestow more abundant honour upon?
options: Those members which we think to be less honourable
Those members which are most visible
Those members which are the most useful
questions.correctAnswer: Those members which we think to be less honourable
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:23 states that "those members of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour" indicating the less esteemed parts receive greater honour.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 12:24, why do the comely parts have no need of honour?
options: Because God hath tempered the body together giving more abundant honour to the part which lacked
Because they are naturally honoured by all
Because they are the most visible parts
Because they are the strongest parts
questions.correctAnswer: Because God hath tempered the body together giving more abundant honour to the part which lacked
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:24 explains that "our comely parts have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked" meaning the honour is distributed by God's design.

questions.question: What is the purpose of God tempering the body together as mentioned in 1 Corinthians 12:25?
options: That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another
That the strongest members rule over the others
That the body may grow in number
That the body might perform miracles
questions.correctAnswer: That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:25 states that God tempered the body so "there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another," emphasizing unity and mutual concern.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12:26, what happens when one member of the body suffers?
options: All the members suffer with it
Only the suffering member is affected
The body separates the suffering member
questions.correctAnswer: All the members suffer with it
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:26 says "whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it," showing shared experience among members.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 12:27, how does Paul describe the believers collectively?
options: Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular
Now ye are the temple of the Holy Ghost
Now ye are the branches of the vine
Now ye are the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:27 states "Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular," identifying believers as parts of Christ's body.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed by Paul in 1 Corinthians 12:28 as a role or gift God has appointed in the church?
questions.correctAnswer: Evangelists
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:28 lists "first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues," but does not mention evangelists specifically.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'tempered' (used in 1 Corinthians 12:24) most accurately mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To blend or combine harmoniously
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 12:24, 'tempered' (Greek: 'symmetréō') means to blend or combine harmoniously, indicating God’s act of fitting parts together for unity.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Corinthians 12:14-27 to illustrate the church?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Paul uses the metaphor of the human body to represent the church, as shown throughout 1 Corinthians 12:14-27, where various body parts symbolize different members.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to the concept of unity and diverse gifting in 1 Corinthians 12:12-27?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 133:1
questions.explanation: Psalm 133:1 speaks of brethren dwelling together in unity, echoing the theme of unity in diversity found in 1 Corinthians 12:12-27.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the teaching of 1 Corinthians 12:4-11 about spiritual gifts?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 12:6-8
questions.explanation: Romans 12:6-8 lists spiritual gifts and their diversity, paralleling the teaching of 1 Corinthians 12:4-11 about manifestations of the Spirit.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes the statement in 1 Corinthians 12:23 about bestowing more abundant honour on less honourable members?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 12:22
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:22 precedes verse 23 and discusses how the members which seem to be more feeble are necessary, leading into verse 23’s statement on honour.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'more excellent way' in 1 Corinthians 12:31 in the context of the chapter?
options: It introduces the teaching on love in chapter 13
It refers to the best spiritual gifts only
It means the way of miracles
It indicates a political leadership path
questions.correctAnswer: It introduces the teaching on love in chapter 13
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:31 ends by pointing to 'a more excellent way,' which is the love chapter (1 Corinthians 13) immediately following, emphasizing love over gifts.

questions.question: How does the concept of 'no schism' in 1 Corinthians 12:25 relate to the original Greek term used?
options: The Greek 'schism' (schisma) means a division or split
questions.correctAnswer: The Greek 'schism' (schisma) means a division or split
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'schism' (σχίσμα, schisma) in 1 Corinthians 12:25 means a division or split, underscoring the call for unity in the body.

questions.question: What typology is illustrated by the depiction of the church as a body in 1 Corinthians 12?
options: Christ as the head and believers as members
The temple as God’s dwelling place
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as the head and believers as members
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:27 typologically presents Christ as the head and believers as members of His body, illustrating interconnectedness and dependence.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 12:29-30, all believers possess the same spiritual gifts.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:29-30 asks rhetorical questions like 'Are all apostles?' and 'Do all speak with tongues?' showing that not all believers have the same gifts.

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 12:3 teach about the nature of salvation and the Spirit's role?
options: No one can confess Jesus as Lord except by the Holy Spirit
Salvation is by works and human effort
The Spirit condemns those who confess Jesus
Faith alone without the Spirit is sufficient
questions.correctAnswer: No one can confess Jesus as Lord except by the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:3 states that no man can say Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit, teaching the doctrine that the Spirit is essential for true confession and salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about the unity of God is taught in 1 Corinthians 12:6?
options: God works all things in all people through diverse operations
God is divided into separate gods for each gift
Each spiritual gift is independent of God's will
God only works through one operation at a time
questions.correctAnswer: God works all things in all people through diverse operations
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:6 affirms the unity of God who is the source of all operations, working diversely yet as one God in all.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the Body of Christ is taught in 1 Corinthians 12:27?
options: Believers collectively form the one Body of Christ with distinct members
Only apostles form the true Body of Christ
The church is a loose gathering without unity
The Body of Christ is a metaphor without real unity
questions.correctAnswer: Believers collectively form the one Body of Christ with distinct members
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:27 teaches the doctrine that the church is the Body of Christ, composed of many members each with particular roles and unity in Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 12:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:11 shows God's sovereignty in distributing spiritual gifts as He wills to each individual.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially highlighted in 1 Corinthians 12:25?
questions.correctAnswer: Unity
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:25 emphasizes unity and care among members of the Body to prevent division, reflecting God's desire for oneness among believers.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 12:12–13 prepare for the theme of ecclesial unity found in Ephesians 4?
options: By teaching all believers are baptized by one Spirit into one Body
By emphasizing physical rituals over spiritual unity
By separating Jews and Gentiles into different bodies
By discouraging diversity in spiritual gifts
questions.correctAnswer: By teaching all believers are baptized by one Spirit into one Body
questions.explanation: Verses 12–13 teach that all believers, regardless of background, are unified by one Spirit into one Body, a foundational theme developed in Ephesians 4 about church unity and maturity.

questions.question: In what way does 1 Corinthians 12:28 connect to Old Testament offices and their fulfillment in the New Testament church?
options: It lists roles like apostles and prophets, linking to continuity and fulfillment of God’s redemptive plan
It denies the validity of any Old Testament office in the church
It replaces all Old Testament offices with secular positions
It teaches that only miracles matter in the church
questions.correctAnswer: It lists roles like apostles and prophets, linking to continuity and fulfillment of God’s redemptive plan
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:28 outlines church offices that correspond to prophetic and apostolic ministries, showing continuity and fulfillment of God’s plan from the Old Testament to the New Testament church.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 14 and 27 teach about the nature of the church as one body?
options: The church is one body composed of many diverse but unified members
The church is a homogeneous group all doing the same work
Only the most prominent members form the true church
The church is a loose association without real unity
questions.correctAnswer: The church is one body composed of many diverse but unified members
questions.explanation: Verses 14 and 27 teach that though the church is made up of many members with different functions, they form one unified body in Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 12:22 and 23 teach about the value of seemingly weaker members in the church?
options: Those members considered weaker are necessary and honored by God
Weaker members should be excluded from ministry
Only the strongest members are useful to the church
Weak members are unimportant and unvalued
questions.correctAnswer: Those members considered weaker are necessary and honored by God
questions.explanation: Verses 22 and 23 teach that the seemingly weaker members are necessary and receive greater honor, demonstrating God's valuation of all members in the Body.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 12:4 and 6 teach about the source and unity of spiritual gifts?
options: Diverse gifts originate from the same Spirit and God who works in all
Spiritual gifts come from many gods and sources
Gifts operate independently without God’s involvement
Only one gift is truly from God
questions.correctAnswer: Diverse gifts originate from the same Spirit and God who works in all
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 6 affirm that while gifts, administrations, and operations differ, they all come from the same Spirit and God who works in everyone.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 1 Corinthians 12:29–30 promotes elitism by implying not all have gifts. What does the passage actually teach?
options: Not all believers have the same spiritual gifts, highlighting diversity and mutual dependence
Only apostles and prophets are saved
Everyone must have all gifts to be a true Christian
Spiritual gifts are irrelevant to Christian identity
questions.correctAnswer: Not all believers have the same spiritual gifts, highlighting diversity and mutual dependence
questions.explanation: Verses 29–30 clarify that not all have the same gifts, which supports diversity in the church and mutual interdependence rather than elitism.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 12:7 teach about the purpose of spiritual gifts in sanctification?
options: Gifts are given for the common profit and edification of the church
Gifts are for personal glory and status
Gifts are random and without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Gifts are given for the common profit and edification of the church
questions.explanation: Verse 7 teaches that the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every believer for the benefit and sanctification of the whole church body.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 12:18 specifically reveal in God's ordering of church members?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 18 shows God's sovereign will in placing each member in the Body as He pleases, demonstrating divine authority over church order.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 12:24 and 25 teach about God’s design for church unity and honor?
options: God gives greater honor to weaker parts to ensure no division in the Body
God only honors the strongest members
The church should tolerate division to promote growth
Honor in the church is based on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God gives greater honor to weaker parts to ensure no division in the Body
questions.explanation: Verses 24 and 25 teach that God has tempered the Body by giving more honor to less honorable parts to maintain unity and mutual care among members.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 12:26 anticipate the New Testament teaching on corporate solidarity in suffering and rejoicing?
options: One member suffering or rejoicing affects all, reflecting the unity of the church
Suffering is always individual and private
Rejoicing is personal and disconnected from the community
questions.correctAnswer: One member suffering or rejoicing affects all, reflecting the unity of the church
questions.explanation: Verse 26 shows the mutual solidarity of the Body of Christ, prefiguring New Testament teaching on communal participation in each other's experiences.
